name: Familial Progressive Hyper- and Hypopigmentation
aliases: Familial Progressive Hyper- and Hypopigmentation Syndrome

ethnicAssociations: Reported in East Asian populations, but worldwide cases documented

criteria.description: Presence of progressive hyperpigmented and hypopigmented macules and patches appearing in infancy or early childhood
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Skin biopsy showing increased melanin in hyperpigmented areas and decreased melanin in hypopigmented areas without melanocyte loss
No associated systemic abnormalities or developmental delay

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive hyper- and hypopigmented skin lesions with a positive family history and compatible histopathology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may identify mutations in the KITLG gene but is not mandatory for diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Onset of pigmentary changes in infancy or early childhood
pathognomonic.notes: Lesions increase in number and size over time
searchTerms: skin color changes starting in infancy

common.symptomName: Hyperpigmented macules on trunk and extremities
searchTerms: dark spots on body and limbs
brown patches on trunk and arms
hyperpigmented skin on torso and legs

common.symptomName: Hypopigmented macules on face and limbs
common.notes: May resemble vitiligo but with distinct pattern
searchTerms: light spots on face and arms
pale patches on limbs and face

common.symptomName: Mild pruritus associated with pigmented lesions
No systemic symptoms or developmental delay
common.notes: Important to differentiate from syndromic pigmentary disorders

searchTerms: excess hair growth on dark spots
localized thick hair on pigmented patches
small visible blood vessels in spots
red spider veins within pigmented areas
tiny blood vessels on dark skin patches
abnormal dark or light spots on mucous membranes
pigmentation changes inside mouth or nose

rare.symptomName: Nail dystrophy associated with pigmented lesions
searchTerms: nail abnormalities linked to skin pigmentation
skin rash worsened by sun exposure

laboratory: Histopathology showing increased melanin pigment in basal keratinocytes in hyperpigmented areas and decreased melanin in hypopigmented areas without melanocyte loss
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant transmission

distinguishingFeatures: Primarily acral distribution of hyper- and hypopigmented macules
Onset in infancy or early childhood
Photosensitivity with early onset skin cancers

redFlags: Rapid progression of pigmentary changes with ulceration or nodularity
Presence of systemic symptoms such as neurological deficits or developmental delay
Family history of skin cancers or photosensitivity syndromes
references: Huang et al., Familial Progressive Hyper- and Hypopigmentation: Clinical and Genetic Analysis, J Dermatol, 2018
Orphanet Report on Familial Progressive Hyper- and Hypopigmentation, 2023
Zhao et al., KITLG Mutations in Familial Progressive Hyper- and Hypopigmentation, Pigment Cell Melanoma Res, 2017
